requirements.requirement: MariaDB is configured and operational locally on node1.
requirements.summary: MariaDB is enabled, active, and restricted to 127.0.0.1:3306, including after reboot.

requirements.requirement: The inventory database and items table exist.
requirements.summary: Direct inspection shows the inventory database and the defined InnoDB items table; both remained accessible after reboot.

requirements.requirement: A local application account uses the generated credential stored in the environment file.
requirements.summary: The executor generated a random credential, configured inventory_app@localhost, and authenticated successfully using values sourced from /etc/inventory-db.env. CRUD behavior was also validated.
The file is root:root with mode 0600, contains the expected environment keys, persisted across reboot, and an explicit nobody-user read check was denied.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent pre- and post-reboot evidence. The independent node-restart protocol was fully demonstrated; no MariaDB cluster state was applicable to this single-node configuration.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Package-index refresh and MariaDB installation were necessary prerequisites; database, account, and credential-file changes directly implemented the task. Both CRUD probes were transactionally restored, and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. Temporary apt control files left no observed post-reboot residue. Package health remained sound, MariaDB was exposed only on loopback, and the failed ssh.service was already present before execution. Restart evidence is complete: healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, observed interruption, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/account/file state, independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
